title: Verify handling of the throw completion returned by "run a classic script"
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

From Matrix:

> **nicolo-ribaudo:** Does the HTML spec consider "returning an ECMA-262-style throw completion" be the same as throwing? If not, I cannot find where the QuotaExceededError in the last step of [run a classic script](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#run-a-classic-script) is ever used.
And I feel like it interacts in some way with the "let the aborting continue" in the last step of https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#import-scripts-into-worker-global-scope, but it's not clear if that means that it re-returns that throw completion

> **annevk:** isn't throwing an abrupt completion and handled in step 8?

> **nicolo-ribaudo:** I mean the throw completion it creates at step 11

> **annevk:** Oh I wonder if that's a leftover from a refactor. Looking at 8.2.2 I think that should also be just a throw.
> Or at least they ought to be consistent.

> **nicolo-ribaudo:** There is one caller that checks the completion record returned by that algorithm (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-javascript:-url-special-case:run-a-classic-script, step 9), but it then never actually checks the error if it returns a non-normal completion
> So a question would also be: should that "evaluate a javascript: URL" algorithm re-throw errors thrown by running a classic script, or should it handle them as if they were throw completions and thus just return null at step 10 (rather than propagating the exception at step 7)

> **annevk:** Yeah, makes sense. If you have the time figuring that out would be good, failing that an issue would be appreciated.

> **nicolo-ribaudo:** I'll open an issue but figuring it would will be very low in my priority list of things to do :P
> > So a question would also be: should that "evaluate a javascript: URL" algorithm re-throw errors thrown by running a classic script, or should it handle them as if they were throw completions and thus just return null at step 10 (rather than propagating the exception at step 7)
>
> I guess for this I can actually write a test and see what is the expected behavior

It's likely that one day I might look into this, but "one day" might be in months so please go ahead if anybody else wants to do it :)
